findings:
The re-plan fixed 15 of the 16 problems from the first review. A hijacked rocket no longer destroys itself when claimed. The timing tests now tolerate float drift. The control dart's numbers and the cap on how often it fires are fixed, the player's EMP Blast against jammers is settled, and the missing dependencies and plan sections are added. One real problem is left, in the Hacker Frigate's movement tests (the same tests the first review blocked on). The Hacker accelerates slowly, so when it is orbiting the wrong way it needs up to 0.8 s just to stop before it can slide out of the player's aim or flight path. The two "it leaves the cone in time" tests therefore fail with the plan's own numbers, and the "always moves toward the near edge" check is red while it brakes. I would fix that one design rule and those two tests, and fold in nine small corrections, none of which changes the approach. The rest of the plan checks out against the code: task order, plan sections, gate-time budget and hub clearances.

### B1. Hacker cone-escape rows ignore braking
At 720 px, 0.30 rad/s is about 216 px/s of tangential speed. Reversing that at 260 px/s² takes most of a second before the Hacker moves toward the near edge. A simulation of the mover's exact rule puts the exit at 2.15–2.72 s at 720 px and 2.02 s at 520 px, against a 1.76 s limit, and 1.80–2.32 s against 1.67 s on the route row. At 0.30 rad/s the "nearer edge" rule actually gets out later (2.72 s) than no rule at all (2.33 s). The plan's only alternative would be an unstated acceleration retune to about 900 px/s². An unattended builder would hit red rows and have to redesign the behaviour or escalate.
